hello.note: Daytime greeting. Ohayō gozaimasu in the morning, konbanwa in the evening

good-morning.note: The polite form; with friends it is just ohayō

goodbye.note: Sounds final, so it is used less than you'd think. Shopkeepers say arigatō gozaimashita as you leave

please.note: When asking for something, or handing something over. After an item, kudasai also works

thank-you.text: ありがとうございます
thank-you.note: Use arigatō gozaimashita for something that has just finished, such as a meal

yes.note: Often just means "I'm listening", not always agreement

no.note: Often softened: chotto… ("that's a bit…") is a polite refusal

excuse-me.note: Gets attention, says sorry, and says thanks for the trouble

my-name.note: Add -san to other people's names, never to your own

speak-slowly.text: ゆっくり話してください

repeat.text: もう一度お願いします

speak-english.note: Ending a sentence with ka makes it a question

four.note: Also shi, but that sounds like "death", so yon is preferred

thousand.note: Prices are in yen. 10,000 is man (万)

how-much.note: Point at the item and say kore wa ikura desu ka (how much is this?)

would-like.note: Literally "give me …". Kore o kudasai = this one, please

i-want.note: Direct; fine with friends, a little blunt to a shopkeeper

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap

just-looking.note: A polite way to decline help

too-expensive.note: Say it gently; bargaining is not normal in most Japanese shops

discount.text: もう少し安くなりますか
discount.note: Only really works at markets and flea shops

card.text: クレジットカードは使えますか

bill.text: お会計をお願いします
bill.note: Usually you pay at the till, not at the table

checkout-time.text: チェックアウトは何時ですか

breakfast.text: 朝食は含まれていますか

wifi.text: ワイファイのパスワードは何ですか
wifi.say: waifai no pasuwādo wa nan desu ka

toilet.note: "… wa doko desu ka?" means "where is …?" for anything

taxi.text: タクシーを呼んでもらえますか

delicious.note: Said to the cook, it is the best compliment

allergic.note: Add the food: ebi (shrimp), tamago (egg), piinattsu (peanuts)

love-dish.text: この料理が大好きです！
love-dish.note: Daisuki is "love" for things you really like, such as food, and is not romantic

what-called.text: これは何と言いますか
what-called.say: kore wa nan to iimasu ka
what-called.note: Or simply kore wa nan desu ka, what is this?

table-for-two.text: 二人です、お願いします
table-for-two.note: Hold up two fingers too. For more: san-nin (3), yo-nin (4)

menu.text: メニューをいただけますか

beer.text: 瓶ビールを一本お願いします
beer.say: bin biiru o ippon onegai shimasu
beer.note: Ippon is the counter for bottles. Draught beer is nama (生)

coffee.note: Hot is hotto, iced is aisu

tea.note: Ocha is green tea. Black tea is kōcha (紅茶)

water.note: Most restaurants bring free water without being asked

milk.note: For coffee or tea, ask for ミルク (miruku)

sugar.note: In a café, シュガー (shugā) also works

cheers.note: Wait until everyone has a glass, then say it together
